MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR PRIORITY
DETERMINATION AND SEQUENCING OF PENDING PROCEEDINGS
CONCERNING ECF NO. 96
1.
THE PENDING RECONSIDERATION CONCERNS FACTS MATERIAL TO
THE RETROSPECTIVE APPLICATION.
ECF No. 86 asked the Court to "state on the record" whether the asset reported as "FB
common stock" is common stock of Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc. and whether that interest was
held on the dates of specified orders. ECF No. 86 at 4. ECF No. 96 denied that motion as moot
following reassignment and made no finding on those questions. ECF No. 96 at 1. Plaintiff's Rule
54(b) Motion to Vacate ECF No. 96 and Determine Magistrate Judge Davis's Ownership of Meta
Common Stock (the "Rule 54(b) Motion"), filed November 1, 2026, asks the assigned magistrate
judge to vacate ECF No. 96 and determine ownership on the dates of ECF Nos. 64 and 84. Rule
54(b) Mot. 19 10, 17, 20.
1

The District Judge has pending requests concerning the consequences of the challenged
participation. ECF No. 93 requests vacatur of ECF Nos. 64 and 84 "upon the statutory findings
identified in paragraph 5," which include "the dates of ownership." ECF No. 93 11 5, 10(R2).
Ordinary briefing on ECF No. 93 was completed through ECF No. 102, filed October 28, 2026.
ECF Nos. 97-99 are a separate proceeding. They present Rule 72(a) objections to ECF No. 96 and
related requests, which ECF No. 102 does not address. ECF No. 97 9 17 asks the District Judge to
decide ECF No. 93 "on its own grounds, resolving the statutory facts to the extent necessary to
that decision." Plaintiff maintains that request. The Rule 54(b) Motion is an additional request.
Mem. Supp. Rule 54(b) Mot., Part IV.E.
1l.
SEQUENCING IS A PROPER EXERCISE OF CASE-MANAGEMENT
AUTHORITY.
The Federal Rules "should be construed, administered, and employed by the court and the
parties to secure the just, speedy, and inexpensive determination of every action and proceeding."
Fed. R. Civ. P. 1. The power to stay proceedings "is incidental to the power inherent in every court
to control the disposition of the causes on its docket with economy of time and effort for itself, for
counsel, and for litigants." Landis v. North American Co., 299 U.S. 248, 254 (1936). How to do
so "calls for the exercise of judgment, which must weigh competing interests and maintain an even
balance." Id. at 254-55. An order setting the sequence of related matters within one action falls
within that authority.
A judge may designate a magistrate judge "to hear and determine any pretrial matter
pending before the court," with listed exceptions, and the district judge "must consider timely
objections." 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1)(A); Fed. R. Civ. P. 72(a). The requested sequence follows that
structure. It changes no standard of review and removes no matter from the District Judge.
2

The requested sequence permits the Court to obtain the assigned magistrate judge's
disposition of the pending reconsideration request before completing review of the Overlapping
ECF No. 96 Issues defined in the Motion at paragraph 6. It establishes the procedural and factual
posture of that request without requiring duplicative consideration, reopening completed briefing,
or altering the relief already requested from the District Judge. Any disposition remains subject to
timely objection under Rule 72(a).
A party seeking a stay "must make out a clear case of hardship or inequity in being required
to go forward, if there is even a fair possibility that the stay for which he prays will work damage
to some one else." Landis, 299 U.S. at 255; see Williford v. Armstrong World Indus., Inc., 715
F.2d 124, 127 (4th Cir. 1983) (requiring "clear and convincing circumstances outweighing
potential harm to the party against whom it is operative"). To the extent that standard applies, the
requested deferral operates on Plaintiff's own requests. It imposes no obligation on any Defendant
and does not defer ECF Nos. 10, 21, or 45. Without it, two judicial officers could address the same
order at the same time, and ECF No. 93 could be decided while the Rule 54(b) Motion remains
undetermined.
IS PRIORITY DETERMINATION AND THE LIMITED SCOPE OF DEFERRAL.
The sequencing request must be considered before the adjudication it seeks to organize.
ECF No. 93 may be decided at any time. Defendants have fourteen calendar days after service to
respond to the Rule 54(b) Motion. Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1). Plaintiff requests priority
consideration of this Motion, followed by prompt consideration of the Rule 54(b) Motion.
The deferral ends upon disposition of the Rule 54(b) Motion or further order. The existing
Rule 72(a) objections remain pending. The District Judge may determine at any time the referral
and successor-designation questions and independently warranted relief under ECF No. 93. ECF
No. 93 19 10(R1), 10(R6); ECF No. 97 19 15, 20(6). This Motion does not seek a general stay or
3

reopen the briefing on ECF No. 93. It presents no argument on § 455, ownership, judicial authority,
or retrospective vacatur. It does not extend or restart any period to object.
Plaintiff requests that the Court determine this Motion on the papers, state its disposition
of the sequencing request, and enter the accompanying Proposed Order.
Date: November 1, 2026
